obligation: Third-party agent notice to each affected LLC
trigger: Breach of security of a system the sole proprietorship maintains for an LLC (the suite, the accounting service, payroll, or the owner's administrator access to an LLC system) involving that LLC's personal information
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred; POL-01 10.3 requires a same-day written record. The agent must give the LLC all information it needs for its notices
notify: Each affected LLC (the covered entity), recorded by the owner as its manager. The agent may send the (3) and (4) notices for the LLC, but the LLC stays responsible
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the sole proprietorship is each LLC's third-party agent under the management agreements

obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals
trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents: name with SSN, driver license or ID number, or financial account number with its access code; or user name or email with password
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred. A 15-day extension is available only for this individual notice, if good cause is given in writing to the Department within 30 days (501.171(3)(a)). Notice by mail or email with the date range, the information involved, and a contact
notify: Affected Florida residents: Rentals applicants and tenants, Storage tenants, and Storage and Laundry employees, each by the LLC whose data it is
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - each LLC separately for its own people

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida, counted per covered entity
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (no extension for this notice). Content: synopsis, number affected, services offered, a copy of the individual notice, and a contact
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if a single LLC reaches 500: possible for Storage (about 610 tenant records) if the storage system was accessed; not reachable by Rentals (47 applicants) or the employees (8) alone

obligation: Law enforcement delay
trigger: A law enforcement agency determines in writing that notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay individual notice for the period the agency specifies in its written request
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the written request
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if requested

obligation: Written no-harm determination (alternative to individual notice)
trigger: After an appropriate investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the LLC reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Document in writing and keep at least 5 years; provide the written determination to the Department within 30 days after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Possible - counsel decides; never assumed for SSNs or screening reports taken by an attacker

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: Not reachable today: no single LLC holds personal information on more than about 610 individuals; recheck if one grows

obligation: Vendor (third-party agent) notice to the LLCs (inbound)
trigger: The suite, accounting, payroll, storage, property management, or laundry vendor, or the bookkeeper, has a breach of a system it maintains for an LLC
deadline: No later than 10 days after the vendor's determination
notify: The owner, at the security contact registered with each vendor (POL-01 6.2)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - track; the owner's mailbox may be the compromised account, so a phone contact is registered too

obligation: Other states' breach laws
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Affected people who reside outside Florida (for example former Storage tenants who moved away)
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Residents and regulators under each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Check residency of every affected person; counsel applies each state's law

obligation: Bank notice of attempted or completed payment fraud
trigger: A payment request, changed payee, or payment the owner did not authorize; compromise of the online banking login
deadline: Immediately on suspicion; recall requests are time-critical
notify: Bank fraud line (number on the back of the debit card and on the printed contact list)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

obligation: SaaS vendor notice of account compromise
trigger: The attacker used or reset the owner's account in a vendor's service
deadline: Promptly, per each vendor's terms
notify: Vendor support (storage system, property management, laundry platform, accounting, payroll)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual; also asks each vendor for its access logs

obligation: Card processor notice
citation: Merchant agreements (contract); Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0 (effective 2026-06-25), Section A.1.1
trigger: Suspected compromise of card data at Storage or Laundry
deadline: Per merchant agreement (time not set in this sample). Whatever the agreement says, Visa's rules require the compromise to be reported to Visa within 3 calendar days of suspicion or confirmation, through the processor (What To Do If Compromised v10.0, A.1.1)
applies_at_this_tier: Only if card data may be involved (unlikely: the owner stores no card numbers and the processors' fields and readers encrypt them)
verified: n/a (contract term not set); true (Visa clock)

obligation: FBI internet crime report
trigger: Business email compromise or attempted payment fraud
deadline: As soon as possible; supports the bank's recall request
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary but recommended

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom or extortion payment
trigger: Considering a ransom or extortion payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy terms
applies_at_this_tier: No cyber policy today; ask each LLC's general liability carrier whether any coverage applies before hiring outside firms

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 (N55-R02)
trigger: Material cybersecurity incident at an SEC registrant
deadline: Within 4 business days after determining materiality
applies_at_this_tier: No - no entity is an SEC registrant (P03 section 1)

obligation: Federal Reserve computer-security notification incident (N55-R04)
trigger: Notification incident at a bank holding company
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 36 hours after determining a notification incident occurred
applies_at_this_tier: No - no entity is a bank holding company (P03 section 1)

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports (N55-R07)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed only: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; recheck applicability when final

obligation: HIPAA breach notification (N55-R06)
trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI
deadline: Not applicable
applies_at_this_tier: No - no entity is a covered entity or sponsors a group health plan

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d) (Section 889); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - no entity holds federal contracts or subcontracts

obligation: Kaspersky covered article discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies a covered article (Kaspersky Lab hardware, software, or services) in use or delivered
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - no entity holds federal contracts or subcontracts
